units.title: 四级选词：杠杆的支点、力臂与平衡
units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Choose an unchanged word from the shared fifteen-word bank for each gap. Each word may be used at most once; five are not needed.

materials.title: A Small Force at the Long End
materials.text:
A science centre displayed a bar turning about a support. The bar acted as a ____1____, a simple device that could change how an applied force acted on a load. The point about which it turned was its ____2____. The demonstration treated the bar as ____3____, keeping its shape rather than bending substantially under the shown forces.

An applied ____4____ was a push or pull. Its turning effect about the support was ____5____. These were different quantities: the same push could have a different turning effect when applied at another place or in another direction.

The relevant arm was measured as the shortest ____6____ from the support point to the force’s line of action. This line met the measured arm at a right angle, so they were ____7____. The tutor did not simply use the bar’s full length in every calculation.

One force tended to turn the bar ____8____, in the direction followed by a clock’s hands on the displayed face. Another opposed that tendency. Under the stated static conditions, a ____9____ arrangement had the relevant turning effects in balance rather than accelerating around the support.

The lesson also discussed ____10____, force acting through a displacement in the relevant direction. A long arm could trade a smaller force for a larger movement under the model; it did not create free energy. The display named its assumptions, including how unwanted resistance was handled. It supplied an account of a mechanical relationship, not a claim that every real lifting task could be solved safely with an arbitrary bar.

questions.prompt: A Small Force at the Long End: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: turning bar simple device defines lever杠杆。fulcrum支点是位置而非长杆器，其他量不指装置。

questions.prompt: A Small Force at the Long End: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.

questions.prompt: A Small Force at the Long End: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.

questions.prompt: A Small Force at the Long End: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: push pull defines force力。density密度、speed速率、work功不同。

questions.prompt: A Small Force at the Long End: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: turning effect about point defines torque力矩。force力本身与位置效应区分，friction摩擦力不指旋转效应量。

questions.prompt: A Small Force at the Long End: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: shortest from point to line defines distance距离。mass质量、speed速率非线点空间间隔。

questions.prompt: A Small Force at the Long End: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: right angle defines perpendicular垂直的。vertical与重力方向有关未必相互90度，rigid不表夹角。

questions.prompt: A Small Force at the Long End: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: clock hands direction defines clockwise顺时针。vertical竖直非绕点方向，balanced平衡不命名转向。

questions.prompt: A Small Force at the Long End: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: opposed turning effects balance defines balanced平衡的。rigid形状固定不保证力矩合零，其他不合。

questions.prompt: A Small Force at the Long End: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: force through displacement defines work功。speed速率不是力与位移相联系的做功量，mass质量异。

units.title: 四级选词：羽毛的枝杈结构与保温功能
units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Choose an unchanged word from the shared fifteen-word bank for each gap. Each word may be used at most once; five are not needed.

materials.title: A Feather Seen Up Close
materials.text:
A natural-history class examined described specimens of bird feathers. The central supporting part was the ____1____. Branches extending from it were ____2____, and their smaller branches were ____3____. The teacher kept these structural levels separate rather than calling every visible line a hair.

In the specimen chosen, tiny ____4____ helped neighbouring branches connect. Together the linked parts formed the flat ____5____ on either side of the centre. The class could therefore explain a surface as a coordinated structure rather than an unbroken solid sheet.

When a bird arranged and maintained feathers with its bill, the activity was ____6____. This could help restore their arrangement. It was not the same process as ____7____, the periodic shedding and replacement of feathers. Maintaining an existing structure and growing a replacement were different events.

The display also showed a softer kind of feather whose loose arrangement could provide ____8____, reducing unwanted heat transfer. Air held within that arrangement was ____9____ rather than freely circulating as it would in a wide open space. The tutor distinguished a thermal role from the flat linked surface of the other specimen.

Several feathers could ____10____, with one extending partly over another. A complete covering thus had relationships between feathers as well as structures within each one. The lesson did not claim that every feather looked or worked alike, or that one feature alone explained every bird’s ability to fly or keep warm. Its specimens supported a description of particular parts and their roles without requiring learners to inspect a missing photograph.

questions.prompt: A Feather Seen Up Close: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: central supporting feather part定义shaft羽轴。vanes两侧片而非中心，pigment色素不是承力主轴。

questions.prompt: A Feather Seen Up Close: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: branches from shaft定义barbs羽枝。barbules是枝上小枝下一空，hooklets更小连接钩不同层。

questions.prompt: A Feather Seen Up Close: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: smaller branches off barbs定义barbules羽小枝。barbs上级分枝已定，vanes完整片不指细枝。

questions.prompt: A Feather Seen Up Close: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: tiny hooks connect neighbours定义hooklets小钩。barbules分枝可携钩但不是钩状扣合部件名称，pigment色素不同。

questions.prompt: A Feather Seen Up Close: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: flat linked parts sides defines vanes羽片。shaft中央支撑而非侧片，flight活动不指羽形部。

questions.prompt: A Feather Seen Up Close: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: arranges maintains bill defines preening理羽。moulting脱换下空，flight飞行动作非喙整理。

questions.prompt: A Feather Seen Up Close: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: periodic shedding replacement defines moulting换羽。preening保现有羽形非脱换，insulation隔热为功能。

questions.prompt: A Feather Seen Up Close: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: reduces heat transfer defines insulation保温。weight重量非热阻功能，flight飞行不同用途。

questions.prompt: A Feather Seen Up Close: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: air held not freely circulating定义trapped被困住。waterproof防水不表空气受困，smooth平滑不命名封存状态。

questions.explanation: one extends partly over next defines overlap重叠。其他候选无对应原形动作，preening词形不合could后。

units.title: 四级选词：眼镜片中的折射与成像位置

materials.title: Where the Rays Would Meet
materials.text:
A museum eye model used a ____1____, a shaped optical element, to alter the path of incoming light. The material was ____2____, allowing light to pass through. At a boundary between the stated media, light changed direction through ____3____. The lesson distinguished this bending from light simply being blocked.

A ____4____ surface curved outwards like the outside of a sphere. A ____5____ surface curved inwards. These words described shape; the optical effect still depended on the material and arrangement. The tutor did not assume that a single shape word settled every possible lens system.

In one demonstrated arrangement, light rays were made to ____6____, spread farther apart after passing through the element. Extending their directions backwards helped explain the apparent location of an ____7____. That account distinguished where light actually travelled from where it seemed to originate in the viewing arrangement.

The ____8____ named the location where the specified rays met, or their extensions appeared to meet, under the model’s convention. The eye model included a ____9____, the light-sensitive layer represented at the back. A change in optical arrangement could affect the relation between the image location and that layer.

A real pair of spectacles would require a suitable ____10____, the specified optical correction for a particular wearer, rather than a guess based on the model. The classroom account offered concepts for understanding the diagram, not instructions for selecting medical correction. All relevant ray directions and shapes were stated in the text, so learners did not need to reconstruct an unseen drawing.

questions.prompt: Where the Rays Would Meet: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: shaped optical element changes rays定义lens透镜。cornea角膜为眼组织、pupil瞳孔是孔不指展示光学片。

questions.prompt: Where the Rays Would Meet: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: passes light defines transparent透明。opaque不透明相反，virtual虚像属性非透光材料性。

questions.prompt: Where the Rays Would Meet: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: bending media boundary defines refraction折射。magnification放大率非界面改向过程，focus位置不是过程。

questions.prompt: Where the Rays Would Meet: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: outward curve defines convex凸的。concave凹相反，opaque说不透光非曲面方向。

questions.prompt: Where the Rays Would Meet: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: inward curve defines concave凹的。convex凸相反，virtual虚的不表表面凹入。

questions.prompt: Where the Rays Would Meet: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: rays spread apart defines diverge发散。其他候选无对应原形动词，focus可会聚与spread方向相反。

questions.prompt: Where the Rays Would Meet: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: apparent represented object location defines image像。focus是特定光线交会点下一空，不等完整成像对象名称。

questions.prompt: Where the Rays Would Meet: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: specified rays meet/extend meet location定义focus焦点。image像可有形状而非特定射线的焦点名称，其他不合。

questions.prompt: Where the Rays Would Meet: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: light-sensitive back layer defines retina视网膜。cornea前层不在后部感光，pupil孔径不为感光层。

questions.prompt: Where the Rays Would Meet: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: specified individual correction defines prescription处方。magnification放大倍率单项不等个体光学矫正规定，其他不合。

units.title: 四级选词：气味传播中的蒸发、扩散与气流
units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Choose an unchanged word from the shared fifteen-word bank for each gap. Each word may be used at most once; five are not needed.

materials.title: A Scent Reached the Other Table
materials.text:
A classroom account followed a scent released in a prepared room demonstration. A substance described as ____1____ could enter the gas phase readily under the relevant conditions. Its transfer from liquid into the air was ____2____. The liquid did not have to boil visibly for some of its substance to enter the air.

The released ____3____ were tiny chemical units moving in the air. Their irregular motion was described as ____4____ at the scale considered, rather than a coordinated journey with an intended destination. ____5____ referred to the resulting spreading associated with that motion and concentration differences, not to a conscious search for someone’s nose.

The ____6____ measured the amount of the relevant substance per stated quantity of air. It could differ between parts of the room. A mixture described as ____7____ contained less of that substance relative to its surrounding medium after mixing. This did not necessarily mean the molecules had been destroyed.

Room ____8____ could also carry the released material through bulk movement. The tutor kept this transport separate from diffusion, even though both could contribute to the changing distribution. A faraway observation did not reveal that only one process had operated.

A suitable ____9____ in the nose could respond to a chemical signal. The perceived ____10____ was the smell experienced, not a direct count of all molecules in the room. People and conditions could affect that experience. The lesson therefore distinguished phase change, physical transport, amount and perception rather than using the single phrase spreading smell to stand for every stage.

questions.prompt: A Scent Reached the Other Table: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: readily gas phase defines volatile易挥发。saturated饱和指含量状态，uniform均匀非挥发倾向。

questions.prompt: A Scent Reached the Other Table: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: liquid to air gas defines evaporation蒸发。diffusion气相传播非液气相变，condense原形且反方向。

questions.prompt: A Scent Reached the Other Table: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: tiny chemical units defines molecules分子。droplets液滴包含许多分子不是这一级基本化学单位。

questions.prompt: A Scent Reached the Other Table: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: irregular not coordinated defines random随机。uniform空间均匀不表单体无规则动，diluted被稀释非运动性质。

questions.prompt: A Scent Reached the Other Table: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: spreading random motion concentration defines diffusion扩散。airflow宏观携带后段不同，evaporation液气相变前段不同。

questions.prompt: A Scent Reached the Other Table: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: amount per air quantity defines concentration浓度。odour感受不数数量比，solvent媒介物质非含量度。

questions.prompt: A Scent Reached the Other Table: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: lower relative amount after mixing defines diluted稀释的。saturated饱和相反方向，uniform均一不必低浓度。

questions.prompt: A Scent Reached the Other Table: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: bulk air transport defines airflow气流。diffusion随机分子扩散异，droplets颗粒液滴不是空气整体运动。

questions.prompt: A Scent Reached the Other Table: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: responds chemical signal nose defines receptor受体。solvent溶剂、molecules物质单位不特指接受信号结构。

questions.prompt: A Scent Reached the Other Table: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: experienced smell defines odour气味。concentration物质量非感知本身，airflow宏观流非鼻中体验。

units.title: 四级选词：动画画格中的间距与停顿
units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Choose an unchanged word from the shared fifteen-word bank for each gap. Each word may be used at most once; five are not needed.

materials.title: The Ball Moved without More Drawings
materials.text:
An animation class compared two films built from the same set of drawings. Each displayed image occupied a ____1____, one unit in the film’s ordered display. The drawings formed a ____2____, an arrangement whose order mattered. Reversing it could change the apparent action even if no drawing was removed.

The ____3____ concerned when events occurred and how long they lasted. The ____4____ concerned the difference in position between successive displayed poses. The tutor kept duration and positional separation distinct: an animator could change one without simply redrawing every part of the other.

A ____5____ kept a pose visible for a stated period before motion continued. The time ____6____ between specified events was measured rather than inferred solely from the count of different drawings. Repeating one drawing could extend a duration without adding a new pose.

The selected major poses were ____7____. Intermediate work connected them under the chosen method, but these important poses did not by themselves settle every aspect of the final motion. The ____8____ of the completed sequence was its presentation over time, rather than further editing of the source drawings. Showing the same material at another rate could change its perceived speed.

One short action formed a ____9____, repeating by returning to its beginning. Another used ____10____, a preparatory movement that helped establish what the character would do next. The class judged these choices by their role in the action, not by assuming that more drawings always meant clearer or better motion. The complete description supplied the relevant timing relationships without requiring a missing animation file.

questions.prompt: The Ball Moved without More Drawings: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: one display image unit defines frame画格。background背景内容非时间显示单元，trajectory轨迹不是图格。

questions.prompt: The Ball Moved without More Drawings: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: ordered arrangement defines sequence序列。loop循环仅一种重复结构，arc弧形路径非顺序。

questions.prompt: The Ball Moved without More Drawings: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: when events duration defines timing时序。spacing位置间距下一空，playback播放过程而非事件时长安排本身。

questions.prompt: The Ball Moved without More Drawings: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: position difference successive poses defines spacing间距。interval下文时间间隔不是位置差，opacity不透明度不同。

questions.prompt: The Ball Moved without More Drawings: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: pose kept visible duration defines hold停格。duplicate复制动作不专有意停留，loop返回重复而非单姿停住。

questions.prompt: The Ball Moved without More Drawings: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: time between events defines interval间隔。spacing此文位置差，trajectory空间路线非时差。

questions.prompt: The Ball Moved without More Drawings: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: major selected poses defines keyframes关键帧。background背景、opacity透明量不为重大姿势节点。

questions.prompt: The Ball Moved without More Drawings: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: presentation of completed sequence rather than editing定义playback播放。frame是单图格非展示过程，其他词不表完成后播放。

questions.prompt: The Ball Moved without More Drawings: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: return beginning repeat defines loop循环。arc轨迹形状不保证重复，hold单姿停留非全动作回头。

questions.prompt: The Ball Moved without More Drawings: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: preparatory movement suggests next action defines anticipation预备动作。trajectory运动路径非预示后行动作，duplicate复制非准备。

units.title: 四级选词：车辆转弯中的轴距与扫掠范围
units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Choose an unchanged word from the shared fifteen-word bank for each gap. Each word may be used at most once; five are not needed.

materials.title: The Back Wheel Took Another Line
materials.text:
A transport museum used a slow model to show a bus turning. Its ____1____ concerned the mechanism changing the direction of the guided wheels. The ____2____ was the distance between the relevant front and back wheel axes. It differed from the total length of the body, which could extend beyond those axes.

An ____3____ connected or located the wheels across a stated line of the vehicle. A length of body projecting beyond a wheel axis was an ____4____. The tutor used these different measurements to explain why the outline of the bus could not be inferred from a line following only one wheel.

The ____5____ wheels were at the back. In the demonstrated turn, they followed a ____6____ different from that of the outer front wheel. The route traced by one point was therefore not the full area occupied by the vehicle throughout the manoeuvre.

The ____7____ area was the region covered as the body moved through successive positions. The ____8____ measured distance from the centre of the specified circle to its edge in the simplified circular part of the example. A smaller value meant a tighter circle under that description, not automatically a guarantee that every part of the bus would avoid nearby objects.

The necessary ____9____ was the space left between the moving vehicle and an obstruction. Without enough of it, a ____10____ could occur: the body could strike something. The display taught geometry through an enclosed model. It offered no instructions for driving an actual bus and did not claim that every vehicle’s turning pattern was identical.

questions.prompt: The Back Wheel Took Another Line: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: mechanism guided wheel direction defines steering转向。yaw车身偏航状态非轮向控制机构总称，other不合。

questions.prompt: The Back Wheel Took Another Line: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: distance front back wheel axes defines wheelbase轴距。width横宽、overhang超轴段都不是前后轴间长。

questions.prompt: The Back Wheel Took Another Line: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: wheel location across line defines axle车轴。front前部方位非机械轴件，radius几何半径异。

questions.prompt: The Back Wheel Took Another Line: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: body beyond wheel axis defines overhang悬伸。wheelbase轴间长相反范围，width左右宽非超轴段。

questions.prompt: The Back Wheel Took Another Line: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: at back defines rear后部的。front前相反，parallel平行非前后位置。

questions.prompt: The Back Wheel Took Another Line: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: point follows route defines path轨迹。swept形容所扫区域，width尺寸不指线状轨迹。

questions.prompt: The Back Wheel Took Another Line: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: region body covers moving defines swept扫掠的。parallel平行不表覆盖并集，rigid刚性不命名运动覆盖。

questions.prompt: The Back Wheel Took Another Line: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: centre circle to edge defines radius半径。width直径向横宽不专圆心边，clearance余隙不是圆几何量。

questions.prompt: The Back Wheel Took Another Line: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: space moving body obstruction defines clearance净空。width物体本宽不同，collision碰撞相反状态。

questions.prompt: The Back Wheel Took Another Line: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: body strikes object defines collision碰撞。yaw车身旋转可无碰，steering控制方向非接触事件。

units.title: 六级选词：策略互动中的收益与单方偏离
units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Choose an unchanged word from the shared fifteen-word bank for each gap. Each word may be used at most once; five are not needed.

materials.title: A Choice That Depended on Another Choice
materials.text:
A fictional game-theory exercise described two firms choosing among stated actions. The decision makers were the ____1____. A complete plan for the choices available to one of them was its ____2____. The model specified what each firm knew and when it chose rather than assuming that every strategic interaction had the same structure.

A ____3____ assigned a value to a combination of choices under the model. It represented the evaluation used for this exercise, not necessarily cash physically paid at that moment. Calling the value high did not automatically mean that every participant or outside observer would regard the outcome as socially desirable.

A best ____4____ was a choice maximising that evaluation given the other participant’s stated action or strategy. A ____5____ strategy remained best under the relevant comparisons regardless of the other participant’s choice. These were different requirements. Something could be best against one particular action without satisfying the stronger condition.

At a Nash ____6____, no participant could improve by changing its own choice alone while the others’ choices remained as specified. Such a change was ____7____, made by one side rather than through a coordinated revision by all. The test concerned an incentive to depart, or ____8____, under those fixed surrounding choices.

The exercise also considered a ____9____ strategy that used specified probabilities over actions. It was not simply an account of an analyst being confused about which plan had been chosen.

The account’s ____10____ assumptions concerned how decisions responded to the model’s evaluations and available knowledge. The tutor stated them rather than claiming that every real firm always behaved in that way. An equilibrium could be informative about incentives while still requiring further evidence about whether the model and its assumptions suited a particular real interaction.

questions.prompt: A Choice That Depended on Another Choice: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: model decision makers defines players参与者。cooperation合作关系非主体，auction拍卖程序非决策人。

questions.prompt: A Choice That Depended on Another Choice: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: complete choice plan defines strategy策略。response对特定他行动的回应而非完整计划概念，information信息不是行动计划。

questions.prompt: A Choice That Depended on Another Choice: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: assigned outcome evaluation defines payoff收益。auction指拍卖机制不指结果对应评价值，其余决策角色或动作也不合。

questions.prompt: A Choice That Depended on Another Choice: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: given others choice best response最佳回应。optimal最优形容词不做best后名词，equilibrium全局互动状态非单边最优回应。

questions.prompt: A Choice That Depended on Another Choice: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: best regardless other choice defines dominant占优的。optimal仅条件最优不表无论他方，sequential依次行动非占优。

questions.prompt: A Choice That Depended on Another Choice: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: Nash no unilateral improvement defines equilibrium均衡。cooperation合作不必无改进，rationality理性假设非相互策略稳定组合。

questions.prompt: A Choice That Depended on Another Choice: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: one side alone defines unilateral单方的。sequential先后不表单方，mixed混合概率非谁改的数量。

questions.prompt: A Choice That Depended on Another Choice: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: incentive depart fixed others defines deviation偏离。cooperation协作改变与单方离开原计划不同，information信息非动作。

questions.prompt: A Choice That Depended on Another Choice: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: probability over actions defines mixed混合的。sequential序贯说时间结构，optimal最优说评价不指概率混配。

questions.prompt: A Choice That Depended on Another Choice: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: decisions respond evaluation knowledge defines rationality理性。information知识本身不是使用评价作决策的行为假设，其他不合。

units.title: 六级选词：热力学熵与不可逆过程
units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Choose an unchanged word from the shared fifteen-word bank for each gap. Each word may be used at most once; five are not needed.

materials.title: Many Arrangements behind One Description
materials.text:
A fictional physics seminar described a gas without tracking every particle’s position and motion. A ____1____ description used large-scale quantities such as pressure and volume. The detailed arrangements compatible with that description were ____2____. The tutor used a stated simplified model to connect those levels rather than treating a visible photograph as a complete record of all molecular coordinates.

Under the equal-weight counting account introduced for this exercise, ____3____ was related to the logarithm of the number of compatible arrangements. A ____4____ transformed a product-like growth in the count into the additive quantity used in the stated relation. This was a specific statistical account, not a claim that the everyday word disorder supplied a precise measurement by itself.

The system was ____5____ when it exchanged neither matter nor energy with its surroundings under the model. For an ____6____ process within that setting, the relevant total entropy increased rather than remaining exactly recoverable by simply reversing an external instruction. A spontaneous spreading event could not be fully undone merely by calling its final appearance untidy.

A ____7____ process represented the limiting ideal in which the combined system and surroundings could be restored without a net change. The seminar distinguished this ideal from a real process described casually as slow. Speed alone did not establish that no dissipative influence remained.

Energy transferred because of a temperature difference was ____8____. ____9____ named the thermodynamic quantity used to compare thermal states and determine the direction associated with that transfer under the specified conditions. It was not the same quantity as energy itself.

Finally, ____10____ described a state without the relevant net macroscopic change under the constraints being considered. The class did not infer that particles had stopped moving. The account linked large-scale state, statistical description and process conditions while avoiding the idea that a single everyday metaphor could replace all three.

materials.title: A Variant Became Common by Chance
materials.text:
A fictional population-genetics class followed a genetic variant across generations in a simplified model. An ____1____ was one version at the relevant genetic location. Its ____2____ measured the proportion of copies carrying that version within the specified population, not the number of visible organisms with a particular appearance.

New variation could arise through ____3____, a change in inherited genetic material. Gene copies could also enter from another population through ____4____, movement of individuals or their reproductive contributions. These routes were different from changing the proportions of variants already present through the reproduction considered in the model.

Random differences in which copies contributed to the next generation produced genetic ____5____. The exercise described this as a ____6____ process in the statistical sense: a finite set of contributions did not always reproduce the previous proportions exactly. A change in frequency did not therefore prove that a variant had become better suited to the environment.

Natural ____7____ concerned systematic differences in reproductive contribution associated with relevant inherited differences under the stated conditions. A variant called ____8____ lacked the specified selective difference in that account. This did not mean that its proportion had to remain perfectly constant in a finite population.

A sharp temporary reduction in population size was a ____9____. The resulting representation of variation could differ from the earlier population even without a directed choice of variants. When one version reached all copies at the specified location, the model described ____10____. That endpoint did not reveal whether chance, selection or another mechanism had produced the path to it.

The lesson kept population definition, reproductive process and the measured frequency together. It did not infer species-wide biological success from one simulated rise. The point was to distinguish mechanisms that could lead to superficially similar patterns and to avoid treating every observed increase as evidence of adaptation.

questions.explanation: movement genetic contributions populations defines migration迁移。mutation新变不是跨群流入，drift有限随机变化非迁入。

questions.explanation: random next-gen contribution change defines drift漂变。selection系统差异非随机抽样作用，fixation终点非过程机制。

questions.explanation: systematic inherited reproductive difference defines selection选择。drift随机不同，mutation序列变不是系统繁殖差。

questions.explanation: lacks selective difference defines neutral中性的。recessive隐性表达模式不等中性，effective有效不同概念。

questions.explanation: one variant all copies defines fixation固定。fitness适合度非全占状态，bottleneck数量骤缩未必同一变体。

materials.title: The Promise and the Position after Breach
materials.text:
A fictional legal tutorial used a fully stated agreement between two imaginary businesses. The agreement’s ____1____ concerned how it came into existence under the exercise’s rules. Its ____2____ were individual provisions in the written text. The tutor distinguished the existence of an agreement from the meaning and enforceability of each provision.

____3____ involved determining what the relevant words required in context. A later disagreement did not automatically prove that the contract had never existed. Nor did a clear sentence settle every issue about whether a particular legal response was available. The exercise kept these questions connected without merging them.

____4____ was carrying out the required obligations. A ____5____ occurred when the relevant obligation was not met under the supplied account. The class did not assume that every disappointing commercial outcome constituted such a failure; the obligation itself had to be identified first.

A ____6____ was the legal response available for the established problem. Monetary ____7____ compensated a recognised loss under the exercise, rather than simply returning a benefit received by the other party.

The ____8____ interest concerned the position the claimant would have occupied if the promise had been performed. The ____9____ interest concerned the position before expenditure or other action taken in reliance on the promise. These were different reference positions, not automatically two sums to add without adjustment. The tutor examined the hypothetical rules governing what could be recovered and avoided counting the same loss twice.

Finally, ____10____ concerned reasonable steps to limit relevant loss under the exercise’s standard. It did not mean that the injured party had caused the original failure. The tutorial demonstrated a chain from obligation to problem to response, while keeping its legal framework explicit. It offered no conclusion about an actual dispute or the rules of an unspecified real jurisdiction.

questions.prompt: The Promise and the Position after Breach: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: agreement comes into existence defines formation成立。signature签名可过程一事但非一般契约成立概念，waiver权利放弃不同。

questions.explanation: required obligation unmet defines breach违约。waiver弃权是自愿处分权利，injunction禁令是法院命令非未履行事实。

questions.explanation: compensated recognised loss defines damages损害赔偿。restitution返还所得利益而非本句对损失补偿，injunction禁令非钱。

questions.explanation: position if performed defines expectation期待利益。reliance回行动前下一空，restitution归还所转利益不等履约后状态。

questions.explanation: position before promise-induced action defines reliance信赖利益。expectation履约后地位异，waiver弃权不是信赖开支参考点。

questions.explanation: reasonable steps limit loss defines mitigation减损。waiver放弃权利未必合理限制损失，restitution返还不是控制继续损失行为。

materials.title: Two Transactions Saw the Same Old State
materials.text:
A fictional database seminar considered two ____1____, groups of operations treated as units under the system’s stated guarantees. They were ____2____ when their execution periods overlapped. The example did not require every operation to occur at precisely the same instant.

Each group read a ____3____, a view of data corresponding to a defined point under the protocol. The value returned could come from an earlier ____4____ of a record. The account therefore distinguished what a reader could see from a claim that the physical database contained only one copy at every moment.

The ____5____ rules determined which changes a transaction could observe. ____6____ concerned the extent to which overlapping work was separated from the effects of other work. A familiar name for a level did not imply every possible application property; the precise semantics mattered.

In the example, each transaction checked a shared ____7____, a condition intended to remain true. Each then changed a different record. Both checks could pass against their respective views even though accepting both changes left the overall condition false. The seminar used this pattern to show why preventing two writers from changing the same row did not necessarily prevent every cross-record anomaly.

A ____8____ schedule placed the transactions one after another without overlap. An execution equivalent in the relevant sense to an allowed schedule of that kind could support a stronger argument than the mere absence of a same-row ____9____. The comparison had to preserve the relationships required by the defined correctness claim.

If the protocol rejected a transaction, the system could ____10____ it rather than present its unaccepted updates as completed. The lesson kept guarantees and application conditions explicit. It did not infer that a database was unsafe in every use because one isolation level permitted a particular anomaly, nor that storing multiple versions alone solved all questions of concurrent correctness.

questions.explanation: operation groups units defines transactions事务。locks锁为机制非操作单元，version版本数据状态不同。

questions.explanation: earlier record state defines version版本。snapshot整体一致视图非单记录历版，write写动作不同。

questions.explanation: rules changes reader sees defines visibility可见性。durable持久为形容词非规则领域名，constraint约束条件不指可见策略。

questions.prompt: Two Transactions Saw the Same Old State: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: separation overlapping effects defines isolation隔离性。visibility读可见一侧不总称隔离保证，locks实现机制非属性概念。

questions.explanation: shared condition intended true defines constraint约束。write写动作、index索引不是需保持为真的条件。

questions.prompt: Two Transactions Saw the Same Old State: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: one after another no overlap defines serial串行。concurrent相反，atomic全成全败不表执行时序。

questions.explanation: same-row writers clash defines conflict冲突。version版本非写竞争事件，write原形不命名冲突关系。

questions.explanation: reject transaction terminate defines abort中止。index建立索引与拒绝事务不等，不表停止未接受的执行。其他不合。

materials.title: A State before the Recorded Outcome
materials.text:
A fictional physics tutorial used a deliberately limited two-state model. The mathematical ____1____ provided the reference states used to express the system. A ____2____ combined those states through the model’s rules. It was not described as a little object visibly occupying two ordinary boxes in a photograph.

The coefficients were ____3____, quantities whose squared magnitudes contributed to the ____4____ assigned to outcomes under the stated measurement rule. The tutor distinguished the mathematical coefficients from the non-negative chances calculated from them. Treating both as ordinary percentages would lose information the model used.

The relative ____5____ between coefficients could affect interference in a suitable arrangement. This feature helped distinguish a coherent combination from a statistical ____6____ representing a different kind of preparation. Two descriptions could give the same result in one restricted test without being interchangeable under every possible measurement in the model.

An ____7____ represented a measurable quantity in the mathematical account. A possible result could be associated with an ____8____ of the relevant operator. The act and record of obtaining a result belonged to ____9____. The tutorial did not pretend that writing down an operator settled every interpretation of how a definite result should be understood.

A pair described as ____10____ had a joint state not reducible to the specified product of independent subsystem states. That relationship was not presented as a way to send an arbitrary message instantly. The class kept joint correlations separate from an unsupported communication claim.

The model’s value lay in making its representational rules explicit. A state description, a measurement arrangement and a recorded outcome played different roles. The lesson therefore avoided replacing those relationships with a confident everyday metaphor. It supplied all mathematical concepts verbally for the vocabulary task and did not claim that learners had performed a physical quantum experiment.

questions.explanation: relative coefficient phase interference定义phase相位。basis基组不是系数相对角，eigenvalue本征值非干涉相位。

questions.explanation: statistical preparation different coherent combination定义mixture混合。superposition相干叠加相反，decoherence过程不是统计制备态名。

questions.explanation: act recorded result defines measurement测量。decoherence失相干过程非每次获得结果行为的总名，coherence性质非行动。
